key_insight: SLORR makes neural networks more compressible during training by directly regularizing the original weights with simple, stateless low-rank penalties.
engineering_relevance: It offers an architecture-preserving way to improve post-training compression without costly SVDs, extra trainable parameters, or stateful caches.
method: Uses two in-training low-rank regularizers: Hoyer sparsity and nuclear norm.
Applies GPU-friendly approximations for forward and backward passes with approximation guarantees.
Regularizes weight matrices directly while keeping the model architecture unchanged.
evidence_signal: Across ImageNet-1K and LLM pretraining experiments, SLORR improves compressibility while adding less than 8% training overhead for vision models and less than 1% on average for LLMs.
watch_item: The method relies on approximation schemes for low-rank penalties, so practical behavior may depend on numerical stability and hyperparameter tuning.
paper_title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
